recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: The connection between the push for school choice and Pete Hegseth
recentItems.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is among the high-profile proponents of classical Christian education, which has grown in popularity. The push to use taxpayer money to fund private schools is helping classical Christian schools expand.

recentItems.title: Leader of Kenyan doomsday cult sentenced to 200 years in prison
recentItems.description:
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult linked to the deaths of hundreds of people has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 191 people. The High Court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa issued the sentence on Friday for Pastor Paul Mackenzie. Mackenzie is also facing terrorism and manslaughter charges for the more than 200 other victims as well as child abuse and torture charges in two other courts. 
(AP video by Jackson Njehia)

recentItems.title: Pope Leo XIV opens his South America tour in Uruguay
recentItems.description:
Pope Leo XIV Friday opened a South American tour in Uruguay, a country with deep secular roots. The Vatican estimated 30,000 people turned out along his route and at the ceremony. Crowds welcomed the pontiff as he rode through Montevideo in his popemobile before joining President Yamandú Orsi for a formal reception.
 (AP Video by: Silvia Stellacci, Martín Silva Rey and Luciano Paglia; Production by Paolo Santalucia)

recentItems.title: Buccaneers' Miles Killebrew on what goes into blocking a punt and the team's resurgence
recentItems.description: Buccaneers special teams ace Miles Killebrew discusses the team’s resurgence after an 0-4 start, what goes into blocking a punt and more. Plus, host Rob Maaddi looks at coaches on the hot seat at the season’s midpoint and gives a four-pack of NFL picks.
